claims.text: A thin molybdenum interlayer between tungsten and CuCrZr will improve the joint's thermal stability.
A thin molybdenum interlayer between tungsten and CuCrZr will improve the joint's mechanical integrity.
The Mo interlayer mitigates thermal-expansion mismatch between W and CuCrZr.
The Mo interlayer limits interdiffusion at the W/CuCrZr interface under fusion-relevant heat-flux conditions.
Bulk W and CuCrZr layers with typical divertor-component microstructures constitute the initial joint materials.
A conformal thin Mo interlayer can be deposited or inserted between W and CuCrZr during assembly.
The Mo interlayer forms a graded interface between W and CuCrZr.
Molybdenum has a coefficient of thermal expansion intermediate between those of tungsten and CuCrZr.
Molybdenum is sufficiently chemically inert in this joint to protect the interface.
The Mo interlayer acts as a diffusion barrier.
Buffering thermal-expansion mismatch and limiting diffusion reduce interfacial stresses.
Reduced interfacial stress lowers crack initiation and thermal-cycling degradation.
Mo-interlayered joints will have better bonding quality than direct W/CuCrZr bonds.
Mo-interlayered joints will resist crack formation better than direct W/CuCrZr bonds.
Mo-interlayered joints will have better thermal-fatigue performance than direct W/CuCrZr bonds.
Direct W/CuCrZr bonds typically undergo interfacial degradation and early failure under cyclic thermal loading.
The Mo interlayer is anticipated to remain beneficial under high heat flux and moderate irradiation.
The effects of extreme neutron irradiation on the Mo interlayer remain insufficiently characterized.
